title: Business process automation
summary:
Business process automation (BPA), also known as business automation, refers to the technology-enabled automation of business processes. There are three primary approaches to BPA.

Traditional BPA entails developing software in a programming language for integrating relevant applications in the digital ecosystem to execute a given process. Robotic process automation (RPA) involves the deployment of attended or unattended software agents in an organizations environment, programmed to perform pre-defined structured and repetitive sets of business tasks. Hyperautomation, also called intelligent automation or cognitive automation, combines business process automation, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to discover, validate, and execute organizational processes automatically with minimal human intervention.

A business process management system differs from BPA, though it is possible to implement automation based on a BPM implementation. BPA providers typically focus on different industry sectors but the underlying approach is generally similar: they aim to provide the shortest route to automation by interacting with the user interface rather than modifying the application code or database.

Business processes that can be automated show up in many areas including management, operations, supply chains, HR processes and marketing. Good candidates for automation are high-volume tasks that are recurring, time-sensitive, involving multiple people and in need of compliance and audit trails. The primary goal is to enhance operational efficiency, reduce human error, standardize processes and allow employees to focus on strategic tasks.
